evidence.reason: The code at the tip confirms the assertion. Inside the `identity is None` branch the ownership proof is conditional: `if before.get("LoadState") != "not-found":` (lines 1562-1575) runs the cgroup/overlay-cmdline check only when a scope is loaded, after which `stop_rc = subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "stop", derived_unit], ...)` (lines 1576-1577) is issued unconditionally. So when the pre-check returns `LoadState=not-found`, no ownership is verified before the stop. The unit name is derived solely from `run["run_id"]` (line 1555), and the in-code comment at 1556-1558 itself acknowledges that another workspace under the same user manager can own a scope with the same name; a sibling state directory holding the same run id and its own lock can create `crq-vm-<run_id>.scope` between the show and the stop, so this cleanup path can stop that directory's guest. This is an incomplete implementation of the stated intent ("prove the scope holds this run's QEMU before stopping it"), not a new requirement; the smallest fix is to issue the stop only when the pre-show proved the unit present and owned (or re-verify presence/ownership immediately before stopping). The interrupted-boot recovery rationale (1548-1552) is unaffected: an interrupted boot that already started QEMU leaves a loaded scope, which the existing check covers, and an absent scope means no guest of this run to stop. The finding's additional suggestion to bind scope names to the resolved run directory is hardening and not needed for the core defect.
